reasoning: As of October 9, 2026, the current federal funds rate upper bound is 4.00% (set September 16, 2026). The question asks if it will exceed 4.50% after the October 28 meeting. Evidence consistently shows: (1) Fed officials expect another rate hike by year-end, but (2) market expectations strongly favor NO hike at the October 28 meeting (~80% probability of unchanged rates), with a hike more likely in December (~68-86% probability). A single 25bp hike would raise the upper bound to 4.25%, still below 4.50%. Two consecutive hikes (October + December) would be needed to reach 4.50%, but evidence indicates at most one hike remains in 2026. The October 28 meeting is expected to hold rates steady.
